scope: Explicitly allowlisted pre-existing TEST databases, public schema on PostgreSQL; metadata and flyway_schema_history only, including history table schema. No business rows, migration, repair, clean, upgrade or writes. No claim of semantic equivalence.
normalization_rules: Type aliases only: character varying→varchar, character→char, integer→int, numeric→decimal. Preserve varchar/char length, decimal precision/scale, timestamp precision/time zone, unsigned. tinyint remains tinyint; no tinyint→boolean, datetime→timestamp, text/longtext→text, JSON→JSONB folding.
Defaults compared as raw catalog strings; casts, literals, sequences and SQL expressions are not stripped or asserted equivalent.
Index signature multiset: ordered key strings, uniqueness, method only; names, predicates, expressions, prefix lengths, directions and full PostgreSQL DDL retained in raw inventories.
Constraint-kind counts are a limited structural comparison; all raw definitions, key columns, check clauses and referential actions are retained in evidence.

All catalog metadata remains raw in evidence, including vendor-only collation, engine, precision metadata and comments; these are not all pairwise comparable. Generation inventory intentionally keeps vendor-specific representation.

History version/script/success/checksum compared across vendors; dialect-specific checksum differences are expected observations, not failed validation. Each vendor separately checked against current source Flyway line CRC32 and SHA-256.

Not covered: seed/business data equivalence, routines, triggers, sequences as standalone objects, grants, partitioning/storage options beyond catalog fields, runtime planner behavior, application startup, production-data upgrades.
